userStories.title: Credential record and encrypted per-repo store
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist a host-aware GitLab connection per fleet repo and expose only safe credential health summaries.

**Motivation** — gitlab.com Free has no project access tokens to mint per job (deferred by the owner). The read/write split therefore comes from two stored tokens per repo.

**Approach** — Data model (verbatim):
`FleetRepo` gains `host String @default("https://github.com")`. Its uniqueness changes from `@@unique([provider, owner, name])` to `@@unique([provider, host, owner, name])`. Migration `20261216090000_fleet_repo_gitlab_credentials`:

- adds the column;
- sets `host = 'https://gitlab.com'` on existing `provider = 'gitlab'` rows; GitHub rows keep the default;
- swaps the unique index;
- creates the table below.

```prisma
model FleetRepoGitlabCredential {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  repoId              String    @unique
  repo                FleetRepo @relation(fields: [repoId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  gitlabProjectId     Int
  encryptedReadToken  String
  encryptedWriteToken String
  readTokenUserId     Int
  readTokenUsername   String
  writeTokenUserId    Int
  writeTokenUsername  String
  writeTokenIsBot     Boolean
  readTokenExpiresAt  DateTime?
  writeTokenExpiresAt DateTime?
  readTokenInvalidAt  DateTime?
  writeTokenInvalidAt DateTime?
  createdAt           DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime  @updatedAt
}
```

`FleetRepo` gains the back-relation `gitlabCredential FleetRepoGitlabCredential?`. Tokens are encrypted with `encryptToken` / `decryptToken` (`apps/api/src/common/utils/encryption.util.ts`) under the existing `VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (`vcsConfig.encryptionKey`), like `VcsConnection.encryptedToken`. No existing row gets a credential record. An existing GitLab fleet repo is "not connected" until an admin adds tokens (design §6.3, no legacy fallback; koda-wk has no GitLab fleet repo).

Credential store (verbatim):
`GitLabRepoCredentials` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/gitlab-repo-credentials.ts`) is the only reader and writer of the table, through the module-private `PrismaGitlabCredentialRepository` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/prisma-gitlab-credential.repository.ts`). Its methods:

- `save(repoId: string, input: GitLabCredentialInput): Promise<void>` upserts and clears both `*InvalidAt` fields of the tokens it replaces. `GitLabCredentialInput` carries `gitlabProjectId` plus, for each token it replaces, the token and its verified user, expiry and (write only) `isBot`. Either token may be absent on a rotation.
- `resolve(repo: { id: string; host: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write'): Promise<GitLabAccess>` returns `{ token, target: { apiBase: string; projectId: number } }`, where `apiBase = host + '/api/v4'`. It throws `RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing')` when the repo has no record, and `RepoCheckException('vcs_encryption_key_missing')` when the key is unset.
- `call<T>(repo, kind, fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` resolves, runs `fn`, and when `fn` throws `RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid')` calls `markInvalid(repo.id, kind)` before rethrowing.
- `markInvalid(repoId: string, kind: 'read' | 'write'): Promise<void>` sets that token's `*InvalidAt` to now.
- `assertKeyConfigured(): void` throws `RepoCheckException('vcs_encryption_key_missing')` when `vcsConfig.encryptionKey` is unset.

`GitLabAccess` is `{ token: string; target: { apiBase: string; projectId: number } }` everywhere in this spec. `*InvalidAt` clears only when `save` replaces that token. A later successful call does not clear it, because the admin is expected to rotate the token.
`resolve` takes `host?: string`. An absent host means `https://gitlab.com`, so a repo object that does not carry the column (older fixtures, narrow selects) still resolves against the default. A stored token that fails to decrypt under the configured key throws `RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid')`, as `GitLabTokenSource.resolve` does today, and marks nothing.

**How the repo row carries the credential (no secrets).** `PrismaFleetRepoRepository` loads `gitlabCredential` with a select that leaves out both encrypted columns. It maps the result to the optional `FleetRepoRecord.gitlabCredential?: GitLabCredentialView | null`, with these fields:

- `gitlabProjectId`;
- `readTokenUsername`, `writeTokenUsername`, `writeTokenIsBot`;
- both expiries and both `*InvalidAt` fields.

`FleetRepoRecord` also gains `host?: string`, where absent means `https://github.com` for GitHub rows.

`gitlabTokenStatus(expiresAt: Date | null, invalidAt: Date | null, now: Date): 'ok' | 'invalid' | 'expiring'` (`gitlab-repo-credentials.ts`) is pure:

- `invalid` when `invalidAt` is set;
- otherwise `expiring` when `expiresAt` is 14 days or less after `now`;
- otherwise `ok`.

`FleetRepoDto.from(r, now = new Date())` builds the `gitlab` field from `r.gitlabCredential` with it.

DTO contract (verbatim):
`FleetRepoDto` gains `host: string` and `gitlab: { projectId: number; readToken: GitLabTokenSummaryDto; writeToken: GitLabTokenSummaryDto & { isBot: boolean }; warnings: string[] } | null`:

- `GitLabTokenSummaryDto` is `{ username, expiresAt: string | null, status: 'ok' | 'invalid' | 'expiring' }`;
- `warnings` is `['write_token_human']` when `isBot` is false, otherwise `[]`;
- `gitlab` is `null` for a GitHub repo and for a GitLab repo with no record.

Wire the service and module-private repository into GitBrokerModule; extend safe repo mappings and DTO specs without changing the assertions for other fields. Use the existing transaction-aware Prisma client so a later registration's repo insert and credential save share one transaction. Add new store/health unit specs and DB persistence/projection specs as part of this implementation.

**Scope** — In: schema, upgrade migration, encrypted store, sticky invalidity and safe response projections. Out: host validation and HTTP client/caller migration (US-002), broker mint/cache (US-003), registration/check workflow (US-004), rotation route/permissions (US-005), old-source deletion (US-006), CLI/web (US-007/008), legacy credential backfill, token re-keying and background token-health polling.

**Interface** — `save(repoId: string, input: GitLabCredentialInput): Promise<void>`; `resolve(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write'): Promise<GitLabAccess>`; `call<T>(repo, kind, fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>`; `markInvalid(repoId: string, kind: 'read' | 'write'): Promise<void>`; `assertKeyConfigured(): void`; `gitlabTokenStatus(expiresAt: Date | null, invalidAt: Date | null, now: Date): 'ok' | 'invalid' | 'expiring'`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] After the migration, FleetRepoGitlabCredential rows can be created for a FleetRepo, and deleting that FleetRepo deletes its credential row.
AC-2 [integration] Two FleetRepo rows with the same provider, owner and name but different host values can both be created.
AC-3 [integration] A second FleetRepo with the same provider, host, owner and name is refused with Prisma error code P2002.
AC-4 [integration] A FleetRepo created without host reads back with host equal to https://github.com.

AC-5 [unit] GitLabRepoCredentials.save followed by resolve({ id, host: 'https://gitlab.example.com' }, 'write') returns the saved write token and target { apiBase: 'https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4', projectId: <saved gitlabProjectId> }.
AC-6 [unit] resolve(repo, 'read') returns the read token, not the write token, for the same record.

AC-7 [unit] The repository row written by save stores encryptedReadToken and encryptedWriteToken values that differ from the plaintext tokens and decrypt to them with decryptToken under the configured key.
AC-8 [unit] resolve for a repo with no record throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_credentials_missing.
AC-9 [unit] resolve with vcsConfig.encryptionKey unset throws RepoCheckException with reason vcs_encryption_key_missing.
AC-10 [unit] call(repo, 'read', fn) whose fn throws RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid') sets readTokenInvalidAt (and not writeTokenInvalidAt) and rethrows the same exception.
AC-11 [unit] call(repo, 'write', fn) whose fn throws RepoCheckException('provider_error') sets neither *InvalidAt field and rethrows.
AC-12 [unit] A save that replaces only the write token clears writeTokenInvalidAt, keeps readTokenInvalidAt, and keeps the stored read token.
AC-13 [unit] gitlabTokenStatus returns invalid when invalidAt is set, expiring when expiresAt is 14 days or less after now, and ok otherwise (including a null expiresAt).

AC-14 [integration] PrismaFleetRepoRepository.findById for a GitLab repo with a credential record returns gitlabCredential with the usernames, writeTokenIsBot and expiries, and without encryptedReadToken or encryptedWriteToken keys.

AC-15 [unit] FleetRepoDto.from for a GitLab row whose gitlabCredential.writeTokenIsBot is false returns gitlab.warnings ['write_token_human'], and for a GitHub row returns host https://github.com and gitlab null.

routing.reasoning: New encrypted credential abstraction, migration and read-model boundary span schema, repositories, DI and DTOs; security override requires isolated TDD with real DB persistence verification.

suggestedCriteria: When the upgrade migration runs on pre-existing GitLab and GitHub FleetRepo rows, their host values become https://gitlab.com and https://github.com respectively without creating credential records.
When call succeeds after that token was marked invalid, the stored invalidAt timestamp remains unchanged.
When save replaces only the read token, the write token and writeTokenInvalidAt remain unchanged while readTokenInvalidAt becomes null.

modifiedFiles.reason: `FleetRepo` gains `host` and the `gitlabCredential` back-relation, its unique index becomes `(provider, host, owner, name)`, and the `FleetRepoGitlabCredential` model is added.
the serialised `FleetRepoDto` gains `host` and `gitlab` (null for GitHub rows); every other field assertion stays.

userStories.title: Host safety and access-based GitLab client
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] parseGitLabHost('HTTPS://GitLab.Example.com:8443/gl/') returns https://gitlab.example.com:8443/gl.

AC-2 [unit] parseGitLabHost throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_host_invalid for http://gitlab.example.com, https://user@gitlab.example.com, https://gitlab.example.com/?a=1 and https://gitlab.example.com/#x.
AC-3 [unit] isClassifiableGitLabHost is true for https://gitlab.corp.example and false for https://git.corp.example.
AC-4 [unit] With dns.lookup stubbed to return 192.168.1.20, assertGitLabHostAllowed('https://gitlab.lan') resolves.

AC-5 [unit] With dns.lookup stubbed to return 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, ::ffff:169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200 or fd00:ec2::254, assertGitLabHostAllowed throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_host_blocked.
AC-6 [unit] With dns.lookup stubbed to return both 192.168.1.20 and 169.254.169.254, assertGitLabHostAllowed throws gitlab_host_blocked.
AC-7 [unit] GitLabAccessChecker.getMergeRequest(access, 7) requests <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/merge_requests/7 with header private-token set to access.token.
AC-8 [unit] Any GitLabAccessChecker method whose host check throws gitlab_host_blocked sends no request through FleetHttpClient.request.
AC-9 [unit] A GitLabAccessChecker call answered 401 throws RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid'), and one answered 403 throws RepoCheckException('app_permissions_insufficient').
AC-10 [unit] getTokenSelf(apiBase, token) returns the scopes array and expiresAt parsed from expires_at, with expiresAt null when expires_at is null.
AC-11 [unit] getCurrentUser(apiBase, token) returns { id, username, bot }, with bot false when the response omits it.
AC-12 [unit] FleetPrStateRefresher refreshing a GitLab-repo PR link calls GitLabRepoCredentials.call with that repo and kind read, and the MR state read through it is applied to the link.
AC-13 [unit] PrAttributionService attributing a GitLab job calls GitLabRepoCredentials.call with kind write and posts the attribution body through commentOnMergeRequest(access, iid, body).
AC-14 [unit] GitlabFleetRepoFilesReader.list calls GitLabRepoCredentials.call with kind read and returns the .nax entries from listTree(access, '.nax', baseSha).
AC-15 [unit] A GitLabAccessChecker call answered 500 with a JSON body throws a RepoCheckException whose response payload is exactly { reason: 'provider_error' }, carrying none of the GitLab body.

routing.reasoning: Host checks reuse the existing address classifier and HTTP client, but converting the client and three caller modules is cross-module integration; credential and SSRF boundaries still require strict security TDD.

suggestedCriteria: isClassifiableGitLabHost returns false for https://git.corp.example/gitlab because gitlab appears only in the path, not the hostname.
getTokenSelf returns gitlab_token_invalid when the token-self endpoint responds 404.
When listTree requests another page after DNS changes to a blocked address, it sends no HTTP request for that page.

modifiedFiles.reason: every call moves to the access-based signatures (`GitLabAccess` is a token plus a target of api base and numeric project id); URLs in the assertions become the api base plus /projects/ and the numeric id instead of the url-encoded owner and name; `verifyRepo` cases move to `getTokenSelf`, `getCurrentUser` and `findProject`; a non-200 that was `provider_error` becomes `gitlab_token_invalid` for 401 and `app_permissions_insufficient` for 403.
the GitLab reader is resolved through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` with kind `read` instead of `GitLabTokenSource.resolve`; the refresh outcomes stay the same.
the GitLab comment is posted through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` with kind `write`; the posted/failed/skipped outcomes stay the same.

the GitLab reader is built with `GitLabRepoCredentials` instead of `GitLabTokenSource`, and its forge-refusal cases come from `GitLabRepoCredentials.call`; the GitHub cases and the refusal mapping stay.

userStories.title: RUN broker mint, repo eviction and host-aware clone URLs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Mint GitLab RUN write credentials from each repo's connection and preserve that host through clone assignment and cache eviction.

**Motivation** — Today a GitLab fleet repo borrows its project's ticket-sync token (`GitLabTokenSource.resolve(projectId, owner, name)`, `apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/gitlab-token.source.ts`).

**Approach** — Broker and clone URL (verbatim):
`GitTokenBroker.fresh` (`git-token.broker.ts`) answers a GitLab mint with no `purpose` and no `readOnly` (the RUN write mint) from `GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve(repo, 'write')`, with `username: 'oauth2'` and the existing `gitlabTokenTtlSec` lifetime. GitLab purpose and read-only requests stay refused here; feature 2 opens them.
`GitTokenBroker.evictRepo(repoId)` drops every cached token minted for that repo. To find them, each cache entry records the id of the repo it was minted for (the cache value becomes `{ token: GitToken, repoId: string }`; the returned `GitToken` is unchanged). `evict(jobId)` keeps its key-prefix rule.

`cloneUrlFor(repo, cfg)` (`clone-url.ts`) builds a GitLab clone URL from `repo.host` when present. `FleetRepoRef` (`jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts`) gains `host?: string`. `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findRepo` and `findProjectRepos` (`jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts`) select it. `placement.service.ts` and `project-repos-assign.ts` pass that repo to `cloneUrlFor` unchanged. `RefreshRepo` (`tickets/prisma-fleet-tickets.repository.ts`) gains `host?: string` from its select. The attribution and files reader already receive a `FleetRepoRef`. Every GitLab read path passes `host` through to `resolve`, whose `https://gitlab.com` default covers a missing value.

AC-authoritative clone fallback: for a GitLab repo without host, cloneUrlFor still builds from cfg.gitlabApiUrl as today; GitHub always builds from cfg.githubApiUrl whatever host holds. This clone helper fallback is separate from credential resolve's gitlab.com fallback. Include path prefixes and GitLab subgroup owner paths without putting credentials into the URL. Coordinate RefreshRepo's select with US-002, where its consumer migrates. Update broker specs, purpose specs and sync.service.token-purpose.spec.ts construction mocks to GitLabRepoCredentials while retaining every existing GitHub/purpose/readOnly/TTL regression assertion. Update exact host-select tests and assignment integration so a stored custom host reaches the ASSIGN cloneUrl. Missing per-repo credentials become the fixed mint error gitlab_credentials_missing; do not use a legacy fallback.

**Scope** — In: RUN write mint, repo-aware cache values and evictRepo, FleetRepoRef/narrow selects, clone URL and assignment host propagation. Out: encrypted store (US-001), access checker/read callers (US-002), registration (US-004), invoking eviction on rotation (US-005), old-source deletion (US-006), REVIEW/FIX/AGENT and purpose/read-only GitLab mints, runner forge identity and opening project-code GitLab gates.

**Interface** — `GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve(repo, 'write')`; `GitTokenBroker.evictRepo(repoId)`; cache value `{ token: GitToken, repoId: string }`; `cloneUrlFor(repo, cfg)`; `FleetRepoRef` gains `host?: string`. Returned `GitToken` and existing `mint`, `evict(jobId)` and cache-key semantics remain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] GitTokenBroker.mint for a GitLab repo with no purpose and no readOnly returns the token from GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve(repo, 'write') with username: 'oauth2'.
AC-2 [unit] GitTokenBroker.mint for a GitLab repo with purpose: 'read' returns { ok: false } with reason provider_error and does not call GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve.
AC-3 [unit] A GitLab mint whose resolve throws gitlab_credentials_missing returns { ok: false } with reason gitlab_credentials_missing.
AC-4 [unit] After evictRepo(repoId), the next mint for a job on that repo calls GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve again instead of returning the cached token.
AC-5 [unit] evictRepo(repoId) leaves cached tokens of jobs on other repos in place: their next mint returns the cached token without calling resolve.
AC-6 [unit] cloneUrlFor({ provider: 'gitlab', host: 'https://gitlab.example.com/gl', owner: 'g/sub', name: 'app' }, cfg) returns https://gitlab.example.com/gl/g/sub/app.git.
AC-7 [unit] cloneUrlFor for a GitLab repo without host returns the URL built from cfg.gitlabApiUrl, as today.
AC-8 [unit] cloneUrlFor for a GitHub repo returns the URL built from cfg.githubApiUrl, whatever host holds.
AC-9 [integration] A job assigned on a GitLab repo whose row has host https://gitlab.example.com carries clone URL https://gitlab.example.com/<owner>/<name>.git in its assign payload.
AC-10 [unit] GitTokenBroker.mint for a GitLab repo with readOnly: true and no purpose returns { ok: false } and does not call GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve.

routing.reasoning: Credential cache isolation and invalidation span minting, repo projections and assignment; strict TDD protects read/write refusal and GitHub compatibility.

suggestedCriteria: When a GitLab RUN write token is cached, a later readOnly request for that job still returns provider_error without returning the cached token.
When evict(jobId) runs after cache entries gain repoId metadata, it still removes all purpose/epoch/read-only entries with that job prefix and leaves other jobs cached.

modifiedFiles.reason: the GitLab write mint is answered from `GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve(repo, 'write')` instead of `GitLabTokenSource.resolve(projectId, owner, name)`; the `username: 'oauth2'`, TTL and purpose/read-only refusal assertions stay.
the broker's third constructor argument becomes a `GitLabRepoCredentials` mock instead of a `GitLabTokenSource` mock; every purpose assertion stays.
the `GitTokenBroker` it builds takes a `GitLabRepoCredentials` mock instead of a `GitLabTokenSource` mock; every token-purpose assertion stays.

userStories.title: GitLab registration, safe approval input and reachability check
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register and check GitLab repos using verified per-repo tokens, host and numeric project identity, with safe approval redaction and human-account warnings.

**Motivation** — That gives one token for every purpose, one GitLab repo per project, and one global GitLab URL (`VCS_GITLAB_API_URL`).

**Approach** — Registration and check (verbatim):
`CreateFleetRepoDto` gains, for `provider: 'gitlab'` only:

- `host?: string`;
- `readToken: string` and `writeToken: string`, both 1 to 512 characters and never returned;
- `confirmBotAccount?: boolean`.

A GitHub create that carries any of these fields gets 400 `fleet.repoGitlabFieldsOnGitHub`. A GitLab create without both tokens gets 400 from validation.

`FleetReposService.prepareCreate` verifies a GitLab repo before its transaction, in this order (first failure wins, each a `RepoCheckException` 422):

1. Host: `parseGitLabHost`, then `isClassifiableGitLabHost`, then `assertGitLabHostAllowed`.
2. `GET /personal_access_tokens/self` with each token. For the write token the scopes must include both `api` and `write_repository`, otherwise `gitlab_scope_missing`. For the read token the scopes must include `read_api` and `read_repository`, otherwise `gitlab_scope_missing`. A read token that also has `api` or `write_repository` is refused with `gitlab_read_token_writable`. `expires_at` gives the expiry.
3. `GET /user` with each token gives `{ id, username, bot }`.
4. `GET /projects/<url-encoded owner/name>` with the write token. Developer access or above is needed, otherwise `gitlab_access_insufficient`. The response gives the canonical path, `default_branch` and the numeric `id`.
5. `GET /projects/<id>` with the read token must answer 200, otherwise `gitlab_read_token_no_access`.

`writeTokenIsBot` is true when any of these hold:

- `/user` answered `bot: true` for the write token;
- its username equals `fleetConfig.gitlabBotName`;
- `confirmBotAccount` is true.

`prepareCreate` calls `GitLabRepoCredentials.assertKeyConfigured()` before step 1, so a missing key costs no outbound call. Inside the existing `txManager.run` closure, `GitLabRepoCredentials.save(row.id, …)` runs right after `repo.create`. The response is then built from `repo.findById(row.id)`, so the create response carries `gitlab`, including `warnings`.

When it is false the save still succeeds (owner decision: allow with a warning). The `fleet.repo.create` audit summary becomes `registered gitlab; write token belongs to a person (<username>)` instead of `registered gitlab`.

`FleetRepoDto` gains `host: string` and `gitlab: { projectId: number; readToken: GitLabTokenSummaryDto; writeToken: GitLabTokenSummaryDto & { isBot: boolean }; warnings: string[] } | null`:

- `GitLabTokenSummaryDto` is `{ username, expiresAt: string | null, status: 'ok' | 'invalid' | 'expiring' }`;
- `warnings` is `['write_token_human']` when `isBot` is false, otherwise `[]`;
- `gitlab` is `null` for a GitHub repo and for a GitLab repo with no record.

`FleetReposService.prepareCheck` for a GitLab repo re-runs steps 2, 4 and 5 against the stored tokens and the stored `gitlabProjectId`, using `GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve` and the client directly. It does not use `call`, so `prepare` writes nothing. The existing returned closure compares the re-read row with `row` using `isDeepStrictEqual`. That comparison now leaves out `gitlabCredential` on both sides, so a token marked invalid by another caller in between does not turn the check into a conflict. When the verdict is `gitlab_token_invalid` for a token kind, the closure calls `GitLabRepoCredentials.markInvalid(repoId, kind)` after that comparison and before returning the result. It does not run step 3 and writes nothing else.

Approval redaction, verbatim relevant create contract:
Both secret-bearing routes register `redeem.redact` with `redactSecret` (`apps/api/src/approvals/route/redact-secret.ts`), exactly as `provider-credential-route.commands.ts` does, so no approval request row ever stores a token:
- `fleet.repo.create` redacts `readToken` and `writeToken`.

Target service constructor (verbatim): the constructor parameters are, in order: `repo` (`FLEET_REPO_REPOSITORY`), `github` (`GitHubAppClient`), `gitlab` (`GitLabAccessChecker`), `credentials` (`GitLabRepoCredentials`, replacing `GitLabTokenSource`), `broker` (`GitTokenBroker`, added for `evictRepo`), `fleetConfig` (`@Inject(FLEET_CFG)` `Pick<IFleetConfig, 'gitlabBotName'>`, added), `activity`, `txManager`, `audit`, `permissions`. GitLab create and check run the verification above. `findByIdentity` keeps its signature and matches any host for now (feature 4 adds host matching to the flow entry).

Use the DTO projection created in US-001; do not duplicate secret read paths. The response's readToken/writeToken names under gitlab are summary objects, never supplied plaintext fields. Preserve GitHub create/check behavior, P2002 conflict behavior and before-transaction HTTP. Preserve the existing GitHub approval regression assertions as well; the current engine treats redeem as command-wide, so the redaction/unchanged-GitHub tension identified in analysis must be clarified rather than worked around by changing expected GitHub outcomes. Update every construction fixture listed in the analysis, plus repo route command parse/run and integration GitLab cases: remove VcsConnection seeding, supply two tokens and stub target forge calls. Keep the invisible-repo case 422 with the new read-access reason. Add API en/zh fleet.repoGitlabFieldsOnGitHub. After the API contract changes in US-004 and US-005, `bun run generate` from the repo root regenerates `openapi.json` and `apps/cli/src/generated/`, which US-007 uses.

**Scope** — In: create DTO/verification, bot detection/audit/warnings, reachability prepare/closure behavior, create redaction, fixture adaptation, API messages and generated create/response contract. Out: store schema/projection internals (US-001), host/client implementation (US-002), mint/cache/clone behavior (US-003), rotation route/catalog (US-005), old-source deletion (US-006), CLI/web (US-007/008), retries and host-aware flow identity matching.

**Interface** — `host?: string`; `readToken: string`; `writeToken: string`; `confirmBotAccount?: boolean` on CreateFleetRepoDto for GitLab; `FleetRepoDto.from(r, now = new Date())`; existing `prepareCreate` and `prepareCheck` return deferred closures, with no database write in the HTTP preparation phase.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] POST /api/fleet/repos with provider: 'github' and a readToken answers 400 with the fleet.repoGitlabFieldsOnGitHub message and creates no row.
AC-2 [unit] prepareCreate for GitLab with host http://gitlab.example.com throws gitlab_host_invalid before any GitLabAccessChecker call.
AC-3 [unit] prepareCreate for GitLab with host https://git.corp.example throws gitlab_host_unclassified before any GitLabAccessChecker call.
AC-4 [unit] prepareCreate for GitLab with no host verifies against https://gitlab.com/api/v4.

AC-5 [unit] A write token whose getTokenSelf scopes lack write_repository or api, or a read token whose scopes lack read_api or read_repository, makes prepareCreate throw gitlab_scope_missing before GitLabRepoCredentials.save is called.
AC-6 [unit] A read token whose getTokenSelf scopes are ['read_api', 'read_repository', 'api'] makes prepareCreate throw gitlab_read_token_writable.
AC-7 [unit] A write token whose findProject access level is 20 makes prepareCreate throw gitlab_access_insufficient.
AC-8 [unit] A read token for which findProject(apiBase, readToken, <project id>) throws repo_not_found makes prepareCreate throw gitlab_read_token_no_access.

AC-9 [integration] A successful GitLab create stores a FleetRepo with the canonical owner, name and default branch from findProject, and the given host. It also stores a credential record whose gitlabProjectId, token usernames and expiries come from the verification calls.

AC-10 [unit] A write token whose getCurrentUser answers bot: false with a username other than fleetConfig.gitlabBotName, and no confirmBotAccount, is saved with writeTokenIsBot false. The fleet.repo.create audit summary is registered gitlab; write token belongs to a person (<username>).

userStories.title: Permission-gated GitLab credential rotation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Rotate either or both per-repo GitLab tokens through a high-risk global permission and secret-redacted approval route, invalidating cached mints on success.

**Motivation** — gitlab.com Free has no project access tokens to mint per job (deferred by the owner). The read/write split therefore comes from two stored tokens per repo.

**Approach** — Rotation (verbatim):
`PATCH /fleet/repos/:id/gitlab-credentials` with `{ readToken?, writeToken?, confirmBotAccount? }`:

- At least one token is required, otherwise 400 `fleet.repoGitlabCredentialsEmpty`.
- The route needs the new global catalog key `fleet.repo.credentials.update`, tier `high` through the `fleet.repo.` prefix in `HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES`.
- The host check (step 1) runs on the stored host. Then each supplied token gets exactly these calls:
  - new write token: `getTokenSelf` with the write-scope rule, `getCurrentUser`, and `findProject(apiBase, token, <stored gitlabProjectId>)`. Developer access or above is needed, otherwise `gitlab_access_insufficient`; a `repo_not_found` becomes `gitlab_project_mismatch`.
  - new read token: `getTokenSelf` with the read-scope and not-writable rules, `getCurrentUser`, and `findProject(apiBase, token, <stored gitlabProjectId>)`. A `repo_not_found` becomes `gitlab_read_token_no_access`.
- Rotation goes through the same approval route machinery as the other repo writes. It adds `FLEET_REPO_ROUTE_VARIANTS.gitlabCredentials = 'rest:fleet-repos.gitlab-credentials'`, the controller route in `fleet-repos.controller.ts`, and `'fleet.repo.credentials.update': ['global']` in the scope map of `permissions/catalog.ts`.
- On success it calls `GitLabRepoCredentials.save`, then `GitTokenBroker.evictRepo(repoId)`, and records audit `fleet.repo.credentials.update` with summary `read token replaced`, `write token replaced` or `read and write tokens replaced`.
- A GitHub repo gets 400 `fleet.repoNotGitlab`.

Approval redaction (verbatim):
Both secret-bearing routes register `redeem.redact` with `redactSecret` (`apps/api/src/approvals/route/redact-secret.ts`), exactly as `provider-credential-route.commands.ts` does, so no approval request row ever stores a token:
- `fleet.repo.credentials.update` redacts whichever tokens are present.

Reuse the registration rules exactly: assertKeyConfigured before outbound calls; stored-host parsing, classifiability and all-address safety; write scopes api + write_repository; read scopes read_api + read_repository and neither api nor write_repository; getCurrentUser metadata; bot flag OR exact fleetConfig.gitlabBotName equality OR confirmBotAccount. Validate supplied token fields through UpdateGitlabCredentialsDto and leave absent token fields absent; registration's explicit 1..512-character contract is owned by CreateFleetRepoDto. Preserve untouched token and metadata/invalidity, and clear invalidity only for the replaced kind through save. Shared client 401 maps to gitlab_token_invalid, 403 to app_permissions_insufficient; no verification failure mutates saved credentials or evicts cache. No HTTP inside the mutating transaction. Integrate RequiresGuard/Requires, ApprovalGated, routeGate.run with global scope, pending response and normal safe FleetRepoDto response, following the existing fix-unprotected route. Add UpdateGitlabCredentialsDto and FleetReposService.rotateGitlabCredentials, and redact parsed patch tokens without inserting keys for absent ones.

Update permissions/catalog.spec.ts closed lists, role-matrix.json (every role gains the same cell values as fleet.repo.create with no other changes), gated-fleet-admin-routes.integration.spec.ts key list and permission/approval cases, and fleet-repo-route.commands.spec.ts parse/run/redact assertions without weakening the existing commands. Add one REST row for PATCH /fleet/repos/:id/gitlab-credentials (area fleet/repos, write, global, key fleet.repo.credentials.update) to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv, modelled on POST /fleet/repos. Add API en/zh fleet.repoGitlabCredentialsEmpty and fleet.repoNotGitlab. After the API contract changes in US-004 and US-005, `bun run generate` from the repo root regenerates `openapi.json` and `apps/cli/src/generated/`, which US-007 uses. Concurrent rotations are last-save-wins; both evict. The legacy no-record/project-id bootstrap ambiguity is recorded in analysis; do not introduce a VcsConnection fallback.

**Scope** — In: partial credential verification/replacement, route/DTO/service, permission catalog/inventory/matrix, approval redemption redaction, audit/cache integration, API messages and generated rotation contract. Out: store internals (US-001), host/client implementation (US-002), eviction implementation (US-003), create/check flow (US-004), old-source deletion (US-006), CLI/web (US-007/008), concurrent-rotation serialization and per-job token minting.
